## Intent
Hypothesis: Halide-expressible loop1 (branchless blend) with an optimized loop2 render can approach the streaming ceiling.

## Cache saturation
All measured N (≥4000) exceed the L1d spill at N≈963, so the curve starts in L2-resident territory. At q=0.0, cost falls from 6.277 ns/p (N=4000) to 5.102 (N=16000) — pure overhead amortization — then barely moves: 4.939 at N=65000 (just past the L2 spill at N≈61680), flat at 4.93–4.95 for N≥262000. There is no knee at the L2→DRAM transition; the working set spills to DRAM without a cost penalty, indicating a streaming access pattern. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: q=0.75 sits at 6.40 ns/p for all N≥16000, while q=0.25 is anomalously lower at 4.71. Every series is flat for N≥16000, confirming the N-shape is governed by fixed overhead, not cache capacity.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 14.54 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.25 — 57.6% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. At q=0.0 the peak is 13.78 GB/s (54.6%). The algorithm is overhead-bound at N=4000 (8–9 GB/s across all death rates), transitions to a bandwidth-limited plateau by N=16000, but that plateau sits at only 55–58% of ceiling. PMC attribution (59.3% useful, 22.9% processing, 17.8% discarded) confirms the gap is overhead, not raw bandwidth saturation. The algorithm never approaches the streaming ceiling in any regime.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize the step function's particle loop. The body is dominated by 77 `str` and 35 `stp` instructions that build struct arguments on a 1008-byte stack frame before `bl _halide_b1`; the Halide kernel itself is opaque. The post-Halide render scatter is entirely scalar: `ldrb`/`add`/`cmp`/`csel`/`strb` sequences perform per-byte saturating adds (16 `strb` total), with no vectorization across RGBA components. Only 2 vector-suffixed instructions appear — `uqadd.8b` in a fast-path 8-byte saturating add and `movi.2d` for zeroing. Float coordinate math uses scalar `fmul`/`fadd`/`fsub` (no `fmul.4s`). No gather is present. The byte-granular scatter stores explain the 57% ceiling cap, and the stack-setup preamble consumes cycles the PMC attributes as processing and discarded.

## Verdict
Refuted — peak bandwidth never exceeds 14.54 GB/s (57.6% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling), and useful cycles are only 59.3% with 17.8% discarded. The byte-granular scatter render (16 `strb`, scalar `csel` saturation) and the 77-`str` struct-construction preamble before the Halide call prevent the algorithm from approaching the streaming ceiling, regardless of death rate or N.
